profile_text.body:
Microsoft is a public company founded in 1975 and headquartered in Redmond, WA. Its Power Automate product, which is the focus of the harvested site content, is described as a workflow and business process automation platform that combines AI-powered, digital, and robotic process automation across apps, systems, and websites. The site quotes a customer claiming that a data validation process formerly requiring over 100 people can now be managed by just a few people using generative AI and Power Automate, and cites a Gartner Magic Quadrant for Robotic Process Automation report dated 23 June 2025 authored by Arthur Villa, Saikat Ray, Melanie Alexander, and Sachin Joshi.

Microsoft tracks a broad portfolio of AI products across multiple categories, including Microsoft Copilot embedded across Microsoft 365, Azure OpenAI Service, Azure Machine Learning, Microsoft Power Automate AI, Microsoft Teams AI, SharePoint AI, Microsoft Designer, Microsoft Clipchamp AI, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, and the Microsoft Agent Framework, which is described as the successor to both Semantic Kernel and AutoGen and is noted as arriving in 2026 with native MCP and A2A support. The company reported revenue of $331,839,000,000 for the fiscal year ending 30 June 2026, per its 10-K filing, and trades on a public exchange under the ticker MSFT with SEC CIK 0000789019.

Microsoft appears as a named defendant in two federal cases in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York: The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, and Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc., both of which also involve OpenAI.
